    StartersAdrian's aranciniCrisp fried risotto balls with peas, parmesan and a melting mozzarella centre, with warm tomato sauceHow to make it20g butter1 onion, finely diced250g arborio rice750ml vegetable stock, hot40g parmesan, grated80g frozen peas100g mozzarella, in 12 cubes50g plain flour2 eggs, beaten100g dried breadcrumbs1 L vegetable oil, for frying250ml tomato passata1 garlic clove, crushed4 basil leavessalt and pepper, to tasteMelt the butter and soften the onion. Stir in the rice, then add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, until the rice is tender.Stir in the parmesan, peas and salt and pepper. Spread on a tray and chill until firm.Roll into 12 balls, pushing a cube of mozzarella into the middle of each and sealing it in.Roll each in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs.Heat the oil to 175°C. Meanwhile simmer the passata with the garlic and basil.Fry the arancini in batches for 4 minutes until deep golden. Drain.Serve hot with the warm tomato sauce.Little Marie's hot honey wingsCrisp baked chicken wings tossed in hot honey butter with chilli, garlic and a squeeze of lemonHow to make it1kg chicken wing pieces1 tbsp baking powder1 tsp salt1 tsp garlic powder30g butter3 tbsp honey1 tsp chilli flakes2 tbsp hot chilli sauce1 lemonHeat the oven to 220°C. Pat the wings very dry and toss with the baking powder, salt and garlic powder.Spread on a rack over a tray and bake, turning once, until crisp and golden.Melt the butter with the honey, chilli flakes and hot sauce and add a squeeze of lemon.Toss the hot wings in the honey butter and serve.Fried calamari with marinaraIt ain't about how hard you hit.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsAdrian's braciole with soft polentaThin beef rolled around pecorino, garlic, parsley, pine nuts and prosciutto, slow-braised in tomato gravy, over soft polentaHow to make it600g beef topside, in 4 thin slices60g pecorino, grated40g dried breadcrumbs4 garlic cloves, 2 crushed for the filling, 2 sliced for the gravy1 bunch flat-leaf parsley, chopped30g pine nuts, toasted4 slices of prosciutto2 tbsp olive oil1 onion, diced1.4 L tomato passata1 bunch basil200g instant polenta1 L water40g butter40g parmesan, gratedsalt and pepper, to tasteMix the pecorino, breadcrumbs, crushed garlic, parsley, pine nuts and pepper.Pound the beef slices thin between baking paper. Lay a slice of prosciutto on each, spread with the filling, roll up tightly and tie with kitchen string.Brown the rolls all over in the oil in a heavy pot. Lift out.Soften the onion and sliced garlic in the same pot, add the passata and half the basil, return the rolls and simmer, covered, on low, turning now and then.Bring the water to the boil with salt, whisk in the polenta and cook, stirring, until thick, then beat in the butter and parmesan.Cut the string off the braciole, slice thickly and serve over the polenta with plenty of gravy and the rest of the basil.Adrian's chicken cacciatoreAdrian's own recipe, the way she cooked it on Tusculum StreetHow to make it8 chicken thighs, bone in2 tbsp olive oil1 brown onion1 red capsicum200g button mushrooms3 garlic cloves800g tinned crushed tomatoes1 rosemary80g black olives1 ciabatta loaf1 parsleySeason the chicken and brown skin side down in the oil. Lift out.Fry the sliced onion, capsicum, mushrooms and garlic for 6 minutes.Add the tomatoes and rosemary, put the chicken back skin side up and simmer, half covered, for 35 minutes.Stir in the olives, scatter with parsley and serve with torn bread.SweetsMarie's ricotta cheesecakeLight Italian baked ricotta cheesecake with lemon and orange zest and vanilla, dusted with icing sugarHow to make it10g butter, softened, for the tin900g fresh ricotta150g caster sugar1 lemon, zested1 orange, zested1 tsp vanilla extract4 eggs2 tbsp plain flour1 tbsp icing sugarHeat the oven to 160°C. Butter a 23cm springform tin and dust it with a little of the flour.Beat the ricotta, caster sugar, both zests and the vanilla until smooth.Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the rest of the flour.Pour into the tin and bake until set at the edges with a slight wobble in the middle.Turn the oven off and leave the cake inside with the door ajar to cool slowly.Chill until cold and set.Dust with the icing sugar and cut into wedges.DrinksLucky Seven Tiger Bar whisky sourRye whiskey shaken with lemon, sugar syrup and egg white to a soft foam, with aromatic bitters and a cherryHow to make it60g caster sugar60ml hot water180ml rye whiskey3 lemons, juiced to make 90ml1 egg white4 dashes of aromatic bitters4 cocktail cherries3 cups iceStir the sugar into the hot water until dissolved.Cool the syrup.Shake the whiskey, lemon juice, syrup and egg white hard without ice.Add half the ice and shake hard again.Strain into 4 glasses over the rest of the ice, dot the foam with the bitters and add a cherry.Montepulciano by the carafeFor Adrian, on the anniversary.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
